entry.title: Against Debates and Dialetics - sum ergo cogito; cogito ergo sum
entry.content:
All thoughts necessarily need to begin with presuppositions, and the said presuppositions need to have propositions that are in essence non-contradictory.1 Each proposition is nevertheless delimiting in its essence. Negation, therefore, of the said proposition becomes a necessary movement in pure logic 2; following this line of thought, and as Heidegger concluded in questions concerning technology, questioning is understood as the piety of thought. Socrates knew this all too well, and thus the guiding principle of 'logos' came into frame. This essay will then take a sharp right turn and will question the essence of questioning and thus try to uncover the very pseudo-humility that hides underneath.

Let us firstly look into the Greek philosopher Parmenides' thought. "One should both say and think that being is." 3

For the untrained eyes, these words appear to be an empty platitude; for the trained eyes, these words point towards a hall of mirrors with infinite reflections.

To understand Parmenides better, let us first take into question the nature of western thought, which is so far understood within Western metaphysics as an expression of idea. As summed up by the sad prince of pessimism:

"The world is my idea (re-"presentation"): this is a truth that holds good for everything that lives and knows, though man alone can bring it into reflective and abstract consciousness."

-Arthur Schophenhauer, The World as Will and representation Vol.1, E.F.J Payne Translation.

This is also beautifully depicted within René Magritte's La condition humaine 5

To have an idea is to then be face-to-face, which then appears to be other than ourselves; we never see a tree as 'is,' 4 but rather we bring forth the idea of a tree through a form of objectification. This objectification then leads to a pigeonholing of the tree into a bounded 'what' defined by everything it is 'not'. For instance, To make the metaphysical claim, "The tree is green," would then be to neglect the infinitude of thought that makes up the tree. One can understand then that this picture of thinking as an expression of idea(re-"presentation") is by its nature incomplete.

Strictly speaking, experience does not present us with a pure subject confronting a pure object. These are distinctions indo-european grammar, and by larger extend ego-consiousness, makes as it encounters, enacts and brings forth the world. To recognize their limits, we must nevertheless begin from within them: attend to ourselves and to what appears, while resisting the impulse to treat the moment chiefly as something to use, categorize into neat boxes. Viewing things purely through their utility is superficial and thereby objectifying them. The question then at any given moment would not be "How can I use this situation?" instead "How can be aware of it more fully, without making my own act of attention its center?" (How do "I" empty the sense of I-ness?) Phenomenology, through its careful qualitative description of experience, may help us approach this question. And lead us therewith to greater reason, greater heights and better views.

All great thoughts (in my intrepertation) have little to no concern of whatever concerns the zeitgeist at any given point; these thoughts are by their nature free from temporal abstractions and quantities and thereby independent of time. Such thoughts and individuals are then celebrated posthumously if at all. Thinking, from this vantage point, has more in relation to poetry than it has to with pure logic. One needs to learn to hold contradictory beliefs without the tendency to fall to neat conclusions, abstractions, and reconciliations; 6, contrasted with the Hegelian Aufhebung, which requires every contradiction to be neatly resolved to a higher synthesis.

Grace in movement, economy of speech, slow judgment, and true epistemological humility are thus foremost spiritual qualities within a person. This is, however, not a normative claim but rather a way of pointing towards transfiguration, an invitation for 'Transmutare materiam primam in animam mundi.'

True epistemological humility distinguishes itself from pseudo-humility through its relation to speech. Pseudo-humility declares itself, makes itself explicit, genuine humility remains implicit. It does not need to constantly announce its modesty; it doesn't need the loudness of "I know that I know nothing" because it is expressed in the economy of its speech, in its willingness to remain silent, and in its refusal to convert uncertainty into the explicit nature of abstractions. Blessed, then, is the one who speaks only so as to protect silence.

  1. Aristotle, Metaphysics Γ.3-4 (1005b-1007b). He calls non-contradiction the firmest principle, one that cannot be demonstrated, only defended by refuting its opponent. ↩

  2. Spinoza, Letter 50 to Jelles: omnis determinatio est negatio. Hegel develops this as "determinate negation" in the Science of Logic (Book I, on Determinate Being). ↩

  3. DK 28 B6.1. The Greek (chrē to legein te noein t' eon emmenai) is notoriously ambiguous, and translations vary: "it is necessary to say and think that what is, is." ↩

  4. Kant, Critique of Pure Reason A598/B626 ("being is not a real predicate"). ↩

  5. Attribution : La condition humaine, 1933, René Magritte; https://www.nga.gov/artworks/70170-la-condition-humaine ↩

  6. Keats's "negative capability" (letter to George and Tom Keats, 21 Dec 1817). F. Scott Fitzgerald, "The Crack-Up" (1936), on holding two opposed ideas. ↩

entry.title: Is this what ageing feels like?
entry.content:
I spent last week with a viral infection and a 104-degree fever. My muscles, during most of the delirium, felt like they were being wrung out by a particularly burly local phelwan and strung like an Odyssean bow in a bloody, sinuous, mucosal feat of athleticism. It was pretty brutal. What pain does, among other things, is to collapse relative sensation and relative time, making the present moment feel like it will stretch out into infinity—it abolishes a sense of proportion, of the relative importance of this moment in the expanse of your life. Strangely, it can do so without feeling at all malicious.

The day after the fever broke, and my body erupted in post-viral rashes:

’the lord has decided to humble me comprehensively’
‘honestly it’s biblical af’
‘my gums have also been inflamed during the fever’
’lucky you don’t have a first born child’

It’s been nearly a week since then, and I’m still recovering. I did not anticipate that. I was looking forward to feeling lucky, as I was lucky—I had the care and attention of friends, who compensated for my general incapacity during my illness with great displays of capacity.

But I harbor resentment still, a sense of having been wronged by my body’s incomplete recovery. I thought this would be business as usual. The ghost of Cardinal Wolsey cautions Cromwell, in Wolf Hall, to take Henry as he is, ‘a pleasure-loving-prince’. Over the years, I have given my body similar warnings. ‘You will find this difficult, but you must face facts,’ I have said. ‘You are the body of a pleasure-loving man, prone to his whims and fancies: harden yourself, learn to act accordingly, learn to be a little deaf, blind, dumb.’

And now the body has revolted, reasserted the primacy of the corporeal over the ethereal. The thought of a cigarette repulsed me during my feverish haze. But I didn’t anticipate this revulsion would continue past my exorcism of the virus. There will be no more mucking about, the body seems to be saying. Don’t fuck with me, it seems to be seething. ‘You think you are pleasure-loving?’ my body sneers like a barnacled genie, and transports me into the anhedonic sensation of lying on a bed of dehydrated moss, smashing flint against iron pyrite, in a Sisyphean standoff with damp kindling. My soul feels antiseptic, like a hospital floor wiped with phenyl. If I had a scan right now, I’d half expect to see a false thermocol ceiling above my sinuses, with exposed wire, and harsh fluorescent white lights.

My body is lawyering up, laser-focused on communicating to me the problem of its continued existence: ‘I can make this divorce very painful, very litigious’ it says evenly, before pausing, pushing back its horn-rimmed glasses, looking down at me through my hooded eyes, ‘or we can make a deal.’

entry.title: Org mode is the best OBTF
entry.content:
• This content is written to be lateral post to r/onebigtextfile and spark the idea to many.

I wrote about OBTF as Second Brain with Org mode a while back, but that post was mostly "here is my datetree workflow." This one is a direct response to obtf.ru, a site that makes the case for One Big Text File a lot sharper than I did, and argues it against FOMO fatigue I've felt myself.

OBTF in some sense is a lazy man's system to get things done. But if you feel more lazier to even think of it, I'd highly recommend to read https://obtf.ru/en website, since it helps me as well to stay motivated to achieve its purpose.

OBTF's philosophy pitch

Their whole argument boils down to a handful of lines:

Your entire life, notes, tasks, ideas, logs, in one text file. Just .txt.

The best productivity system is the one you actually use. And nothing is simpler than a text file.

Search beats categories

No vendor lock-in, speed, offline by default, permanence. All fair, and none of it is specific to a bare .txt file. It's specific to plain text. You make use of many tools to suite your needs instead of you learning and adapting to a system.

Some posts on OBTF found over internet:

  • Forum post on MacPowerUsers
  • https://mrshll.uk/posts/plain-text-planner/
  • https://jeffhuang.com/productivity_text_file/
  • https://mrdizzy.blog/blog/obtf/
  • https://beardystarstuff.net/posts/2024-04-17.html
  • https://whhone.com/posts/one-line-per-day-diary-in-org-mode/

Where Org gives you more

"Search beats categories" is true until the file gets big enough that search alone stops being enough, and at that point you want structure you can turn on when you need it, not structure forced on you from day one.

I still keep a datetree, Year > Month > Day > entry, which gives me OBTF's own "newest entries first, just append and go" model: 

* 2026
** 2026-10 October
*** 2026-10-07 Tuesday
**** <whatever I'm capturing>            :tag1:tag2:

The difference from a flat file is that I'm not stuck with chronology as the only axis. A few things I still reach for on top of the datetree:

  • org-sparse-tree (C-c /): narrow the whole tree down to just the headings matching a tag or property, without touching the file itself.
  • consult-org-heading / consult-line (from the consult package): fuzzy-jump straight to a heading or line, which is the actual "search beats categories" experience, just inside a structured file instead of a flat one.
  • org-ql: for queries that are more than a single tag match, closer to a real query language over my notes than regexp-over-a-text-file ever was.
  • #+select_tags: export just the headings carrying a given tag into a throwaway buffer, which behaves like a temporary, generated "file" scoped to one topic, without ever having to actually split the real file.
  • org-super-links: Package to backlink org headings to one another.
  • org-agenda: Best way to get organized and plan for time. Paired with note taking, the agenda interface is so powerful that even I've underused it mostly to just get stuff done.
  • Tags: More detail on the tagging convention I use (the l@=/=n@=/=p@ prefixes) is in OBTF as Second Brain with Org mode.

Conclude

These might sound very much tied to emacs, yes thats mostly true. Environment so perfect that it can be called a monolith of emacs. But alas, people have ported org mode inspired modes and packages to various other ecosystem.

  • orgmode.nvim: OG clone for neovim
  • org.nvim: New and AI assisted clone of complete org library
  • neorg: Future of organizing life in neovim
  • grove: Beautiful org mode first task/notes android app
  • orgzly-revived: Org in mobile at ease
  • orgro: Good org mode reader for android+IOS

PS: I use official Emacs on Android as well bringing the same environment on the phone (_;)

Ultimately only thing that is required with note taking or system is to always review, revise, repeat and process them.

entry.title: Weeknote 40 2026
entry.content:
A SUPER DUPER late weeknote, well I do have my rote memorized reasons ready, here we go:

  • I was on a trip this long weekend to Sakleshpur, Udupi and Mangalore. What a time, it was so good that I forgot my phone even existed, truly healed! Detailed experience in a blog post entry hitting your reader soon ™️ :).
  • I had a childhood friend over, who I did the trip with! I was still busy entertaining him for the rest of the week too 🐒.
  • And some important personal work which kept me occupied till Tuesday evening.

But after dropping off my friend to the station, I am finally free and hence penning down this weeknote right now on Wednesday evening. 😭

Life

IndiaFOSS second day

I had a blast on the second day of IndiaFOSS too! One thing which surprised me was the number of people hanging around on day 2. IndiaFOSS's retention has improved a lot! It's honestly great to see that because I am part of the stay-till-end group :). I blogged about my experience here. After conf chill

After the conference I again hung out with FP and Rust India group peeps accompanied by Sohom, Harsh and Yash. We went out to The Bloom for some coffee and light snacks. We had initially planned to spend time in Kahale, but seeing a bunch of people there made Anupam's eyes go W I D E. 👁️👄👁️

After the hang out, me, Yash and Harsh had some time to kill and started doing a mini photoshoot session. I have inherited a 15-20 year old Kodak EasyShare and am always trying to find an excuse to use it xD. We shot some really good photos, I think I also got one of the best photos of mine ever, thanks a lot Yash!! 🙇.

Before I talk about my next experience, lemme just state: Food review for The Bloom is in the section below :).

Now that food is out of the way, lets talk about something related to food actually being out 💩. I went to use the toilet and some MF had shat on the jet. That person didn't even bother to clean it. In fact, jet was placed at an angle that I would have never realized there was shit on the side facing away. Whoever did this "shit", YOU ARE DISGUSTING, please do not step into a public washroom ever after, FUCK YOU!

Hangout with Telegram group

After the cafe hangout, me, Harsh and Yash headed to Azuki to meet Akshit and Amogh for some nice Japanese dinner :). Except Amogh, who was my college senior, I have met everyone else in the group on Telegram. These are terminally online people but somehow also spend a LOT of time hanging out with each other in real life. Best combination if you were to ask me :).

Thanks 🙏

I also want to say thanks to all the people who lent me an ear to rant after last week's fiasco. I am feeling much better after venting to enough people 🙈.

Writing experiment

I have been meaning to start writing personal-notes again, these are disparate notes which I write on random days trying to brain dump about work related matters, things I am not comfortable sharing on this website, etc.

I had forgotten I had started this practice earlier too! I only realized this while trying to make a repo with the same name 🙃. It was SO interesting to read what my 2023 self was thinking about. In few of the fundamental ways I still think the same way in 2026, maybe they are correct or maybe I am headed down the wrong path, only time will tell.

But yeah, I am going to try writing these notes more regularly than before, I want to relive the moments I felt reading those old notes over and over again!

Cowork

I got around to attending Nemo's cowork session again this Tuesday! Interacting with people in these spaces always get me stoked to work on new and interesting ideas, PEOPLE ARE SO INTERESTING! This was the presentation section this time:

  • IR for GUI by Ankur
  • Xiaomi <> Samsung contacts fuckup by Tanvi
  • Color palette of movies by Unnati
  • Coffee bags 3D collection by Ken
  • Statistical analysis by Kartik
  • Lowering the barrier to submitting ideas for policies by Unknown

Climbing

I missed climbing on Sunday because of IndiaFOSS, I have mixed feelings about this because I also want to start focusing on strength and flexibility to get past the levels I am stuck at.

Another important observation I have made is, my forearms have been feeling like they have no power. But at the same time I can go ahead and do super strong moves. I find this occurrence confusing, I hope it's not something like Toby faced 🤞.

Tuesday

Another day passes by and the red level 5 on overhang keeps mocking me, PLEASE JUST HAPPEN PLEASE! As if my plea is going to change the route in some way. All said and done, I am going to keep trying it. I AM COMING FOR YOU, STRONGER AFTER EVERY SESSION! 💢

After falling off the red multiple times, I shifted my focus to a green level 5 slab. Most of it was pretty chill but rest of my session was spent trying to execute it's last move reliably.

I talked about not feeling powerful response from my forearms, but at the same time, I sent all the level 3s without a break near the end of the session and that didn't tire me out 🤷‍♂️. Feeling bummed for not being tired, I moved on to do some physically taxing level 4s and 5s without any break and guess what, I STILL WASN'T TIRED! So next, I did 10 normal pulls, 10 weighted pull ups and a couple of core exercises with few sets. At the end, I left unsatisfied with the session cause I wasn't tired 😭.

There are two only explanations for this, my body is not transmitting power and tired signals to my brain, or, I have somehow become even stronger. I would love to believe it's the second, but have no proof 🙃.

Thursday

This was a super exciting session! They changed the first wall and the baby wall and oh boy some of the routes are beautiful!

I was able to flash almost all of the level 3s and 4s which was assuring after the setbacks over the past weeks. The only level 4 I wasn't able to flash had a SUPER FUN bat hang 🦇 at the end of the it! Enjoy my video of doing the same xD

https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/oLC2mREpyr0?mute=1

Next, I moved on to level 5s. There were only two in this set, one on each wall. I started with pink level 5 on baby wall cause that seemed crimpy which is usually my style. I wasn't able to flash it, in fact it took more attempts than I would have loved, but I was able to send it finally and am happy with the custom beta I found for my height!

Next, I moved on to the yellow level 5 on first wall. Initially I was trying to do just the first move perfectly, but once I was able to repeat the sequence reliably, I just went for the second and then the third and somehow I sent it in that attempt itself!! Towards the end whole gym was astonished at the way I completed it cause I caught the last hold with a single hand and pulled myself towards the wall when I was parallel to it and stuck the move and then matched, it was all so crazy I still can't digest I actually landed that move!!! I wish I had a video, that would prove the big injustice I am doing to the exact sequence, but sadly even I wasn't expecting to send the route in that go, so none was recoded :(.

Food

The Bloom, Jayanagar

I had ordered Caramel banana iced latte and it slapped hard. It was really good! Even others seemed to have enjoyed all of their drinks. As we were a decently sized group with varying tastes and most of the people liked their drinks, I guess we can call it a "try if around" place :).

We also ordered some French Fries and even they were delicious. For some reason, most of the places I have tried fries at, I don't end up liking them. It is very hard to make good fries. I don't know if the explanation amounts to something, but that must mean something!

Azuki

I went to Azuki just after The Bloom and hence had a bit less appetite. To keep it light, I ordered simple Omu Rice and milk based bubble tea. Yash and Amogh had ordered matcha based bubble tea which I think was better 🤔.

For the desserts we had Mitarashi Dango, Anpanman and Pancake dessert. Mann I love Japanese desserts, they are all so good. 🤤

All good until bill arrives, this place is SUPER EXPENSIVE! 😵

Amma and Appa

Me, Harsh and Yash set out on a Tuesday morning wanting to get some good south indian breakfast at Amma and Appa. Guess the ONLY DAY it stays closed. 🫠

We ended up having breakfast at Srirangam, and honestly I am not a big fan of theirs, they make ehhh dosas. :/

Reads

  • https://kristoff.it/blog/the-zig-journey/

      • Looking at you Thorsten Bell who thinks static typed systems would disappear in the world of LLMs. It's really stupid someone actually believes this 🫠. Any context which can be offloaded to a rather cheap deterministic system will ALWAYS thrive!

    • Learning to understand systems in depth will make you not only better at using dependencies, but also at steering LLMs. This might seem counter-intuitive at first glance, but it’s kind of an obvious truth: how can you evaluate the quality of what you get from a dependency or an agent, if you have no idea of what’s even possible?

entry.title: DJ Mart
entry.content:
I'm learning to DJ. For now, I'm calling myself DJ Mart. These are my newbie notes.

DJ Basics

There are lots of good resources online to figure out DJing and I won't do better here. I will just say that DJ controllers have a few basic elements that are core to the practice, everything else is basically fancy flourishes on top.

This is my DJ controller:

There's a left side and a right side, with symmetric controls. The whole art of DJing can be reductively summed up as transitioning the song on the left side to the song on the right side.

This is the software I am using that came with my controller:

The software again, has a left side and right side, and the two stacked waveforms represent the left and right. The other buttons are just software representation of what's on my control, and there's a tracklist, where I can load songs on both sides.

Again, this won't turn into a DJ tutorial, but know the bulk of what DJ Mart will do in your party involves:

  • Play one song with with full volume to the speaker (on the slider near the center labelled either "1")

  • Play the other song, but with the slider "2" set to zero, and play it only to my headphones

  • Use sliders labelled "tempo" to get the beats per minute to match (the exact number is visible on the software)

  • Use the spinwheel to position and get the beats to line up

  • Play with the other knobs (most of the time the three EQ knobs in the center for high, medium and low frequencies) to mix the two songs properly

  • At some point turn up "2" and turn down "1", and swap out the song on the left side

  • Rinse and repeat

Doing a basic transition isn't too hard. Doing an amazing one can be pretty hard though, to me the whole game is being able to find two songs that work well together in a way that generates delight. There are some basic rules of thumb (like there are keys that harmonise well together, etc), but for the most part I try to optimise for my own amusement.

I personally enjoy poppy-ish tracks rather than rave or techno type stuff, and I don't worry too much about drops. I try to maximise fun and surprise overall. The measure for fun is "whatever I like."

entry.title: What do I read next?
entry.content:
Finding my next book to read is a major problem. I am currently focused on reading one book, trying to figure out whether I'll finish it, and then moving on to the next one. But what do I read next? When I am already on a book, I keep scrolling through reviews and book recommendations on YouTube and Instagram, and keep adding them to the To Read Pile. After a few days, when I actually have to pick up my next book, I always make a random choice, and it's rarely from the to-read pile. My to-read pile keeps filling up without any books coming off of it. After a few days, I forget why the book is even there in the list. I forget who recommended it to me and why I thought I would want to read it in the first place. It would be nice to be able to add a note to my To Read Pile on my StoryGraph, but I don't really see that helping a lot with the choice of what to read next.

​

But not having a list also isn't good. When I do have to make a choice, if I don’t know what my options are, I tend to take a lot more time trying to make a choice rather than reading. Constantly thinking about what should be my next book is too much pressure, which leads me nowhere. It is exactly like me having to choose a food order from the menu. Looking for what I am hungry for right now in the menu is a much better option, instead of having to choose from everything that is available. Is chicken wings not on the menu? Sure what is the next best fried thing on the menu?

​

This is what has been working for me so far. A book goes into the To Be Read pile only if I get the book recommended to me by multiple sources.

  • How many videos I watched about a book doesn’t really matter, all content from YouTube and Instagram on a book just counts as one source.
  • Second source, noticing what random people are reading on the bus, metro, libraries, parks, waiting in the lobby before a play is about to start, or anywhere out in public.
  • Third sources are books that are turned into movies or TV shows, I haven't seen people talk about this enough. A book being turned into a movie, for me, feels like a validation no one asked for.
  • Fourth source, the most important one, books recommended by a friend. Books recommended by a friend are the highest priority item on the list just because I have someone immediately to talk to about the book. My messages to them are my journal entries on that book.

​

Not having a physical list that keeps growing forever is where the problem is. A tiny note in my brain which only remembers books based on how many times I have come across them is the best option. Looking up the genre and reading the description of the book helps with retention and helps a lot while making the choice. If I don’t know what kind of a book that is, it won't really help me decide if I am in the mood for it. Sitting and reading about the book while making a choice has turned out to be a bad idea. If I don’t know whether this item is fried or not, I would much rather stay away from it. I have noticed that whenever I do it, I get distracted by whether I should read this next and move toward whether this should be on my reading list mode. That again will prevent me from reading the book.

​

The exception of choosing a book that is not on the list is also a case. There are days when I do not want to explore and just read familiar kinds of books. I would want to read new books, but something that feels familiar, I am not talking about reading a book again. This is when I go back to a random book by an author I liked, regardless of how many times I have come across it. Does not matter if a friend recommended it to me or not, does not matter if it is on the list or not, does not matter if I have seen it on my feed.

​

I have stopped consuming articles and videos on ten must read books, or standalone fantasies or any such reading topics. Instead, I am looking for reviews and theories of the books that I have already read. Doing so has gotten me to think more about the book, even several weeks past its completion. Looking at these contents has made me look forward to the time when I get to reread these books. I hope the To Be Re-read list will not be such a pain in the ass.

entry.title: A Day in My Life
entry.content:
Author’s note: I wrote this note through the day, as it happened.

I wake up earlier than usual, at 6:15 AM. My body feels rested enough so I get out of the bed. Not sure if I am going to regret not sleeping enough later in the day. My smartwatch tells me to rest today and that’s my plan. But today is a work from office day. I hope it is not too hectic.

I get ready, eat some carb, and jump in the cab to suffer through the commute. Eggs and coffee later at work. In the cab, I read a bunch of blog posts by the Indieweb Club Bengaluru (IWCB) folks. Browsing through Tanvi’s notes makes me want to write this note. I start typing it in Google Keep. The cab ride is unremarkable. I get sleepy towards the end, but I can’t take a nap because there isn’t enough time.

Today’s weather reminds me of good old Bengaluru days from a decade ago. It rained overnight and the day has been switching between cloudy and sunny. Ten years ago I would have cycled to work, feeling the cool breeze on my face, but the traffic these days has made it impossible.

The cab is three minutes late to the office. That’s okay, we are almost never in time these days. The door to my floor’s entrance has been shattered for a week now. The closing mechanism on the door tries to keep closing it but the rope tied to it keeps it open. The door flutters and sways back-and-forth continuously. I wonder if there is a metaphor here. I go around and enter through another door.

The breakfast is eggs, veggies, yogurt, and juice. I try to finish it, but I’m too stuffed, so I keep the yogurt for lunch. The cafe has a long queue because their ordering machines are not working. So I take the elevator to a different cafe. The queue is even longer here. I order my usual and wait. Meanwhile, I look at people come and go. Someone has a neck pillow. A person wearing dress shoes. Another wearing large headphones. After a long wait my decaf cappuccino finally arrives. I finish it on the way to my desk, and feel bad about waiting so long and not savouring it. I walk through the swaying shattered door and sit on my chair. Now it’s time to work.

All my PRs are stuck in approval hell; comments and reviews going back and forth for days. No new comments have come today so there isn’t much I can do. I start working on the design doc for my next project.

After a while, I take a water break. Walking to the break room, I notice how sore my legs are. This is good soreness, from the runs I did last weekend. But my shoulders are sore too, and I know this to be a result of my bad posture. I should stretch more. The sky is cloudy. I wonder if I should go for a walk. Maybe after lunch.

A new person has joined our team. I have a chat with them, talking about what brought them to our team. They are interested in compilers and programming languages. I think about my long pending PRs.

Write code, read documentation, write the design doc, run tests, check out Mastodon in between. Now it is time for a meeting. After saying my piece I alternate between staring at my phone and at my laptop screen. By the time the meeting gets over, I’m hungry.

I come back to my desk and have the leftover bowl of yogurt. It’s delicious. Some more work while the teammates get ready to go for lunch. At 1 PM, we go to the cafeteria. It is bustling with people. I decide to have a light lunch and go for the पोषक (nutritious) counter. There is a long queue. Everyone is health conscious these days. I patiently stand behind 15 people, waiting for my turn.

Just when I reach the counter, food gets over. More waiting in my luck today. There are 15 people behind me in the queue now. Eventually more food arrives, and I grab some chicken skewers, roasted bell peppers, and rice for lunch. At the lunch table, the conversation veers to the history of the Channel Tunnel.

After lunch I crave more coffee but I restrain myself. There is no time to go for a walk. I need to finish some work. It’s too sunny anyway.

I work work work. After a while, it is time to go back home. I get in the cab and sit back. It is going to take an hour, says Google Maps. It often lies.

Traffic and weather are the two things people talk about the most in Bengaluru. Weather good; traffic bad. But increasingly, weather is also getting bad, and making the traffic worse. Earlier someone casually mentioned that it took them two hours to get home yesterday, for a commute that is usually 45 minutes. I have been stuck in three hour long traffic jams this year as well. It is terrible all around.

I sleep through most of the ride and reach home in 1 hour and 8 minutes. I hope my snores did not disturb my co-passengers. I change and lie down in the bed for fifteen minutes. I reply to the two people who mailed me at my personal email, showcasing their projects. “Looks nice, good luck.” I’m not sure why they mailed me in the first place; it’s not like I’m an influencer or something. Well, anyway, now it is time to go pick up my kid from the school. My wife dropped her to the school in the morning while I went to work. It is starting to rain. Thankfully, I have an umbrella and a car.

Back home in 30 minutes, my wife makes tea and chocolate pancakes for us, which I gladly gorge down. Finally, I find some free time, so I work on fixing a webring related bug in the IWCB website that Yash reported earlier in the day. The fix takes ten minutes and one line of change.

I need to finish my steps for the day, but I also need to do some strength training today as per my plan. However, my body is still too sore. I finally decide to go for a walk. Wife and I go walk around our building for 30 minutes or so. The rain stopped awhile ago and the weather feels really nice. There is a cool breeze and the sunset is filling the sky with colors. We talk about various things, then we go pick our kid from the drawing class.

The colorful sunset

Back in front of my laptop, I spend fifteen minutes reading posts in my feed reader. I check my website analytics, and find that despite my best efforts to keep bots out, a bot has somehow managed to crawl all my linkblog tags. I don’t know what more to do than all I’ve already done. I delete the bots hits from my analytics database. Next, I can either read about Type inference or watch some One Piece.

I watch one episode of One Piece before dinner. Dinner is plain roti-sabzi-dal. I watch another episode after. It is quite close to my shutdown time so I decide to move this post from Google Keep to my website. I edit and prepare it for posting. I download the photos I took today, and add them to the post. I do a round of proofreading. It is ready.

Now we’ve caught up to the present. Here is what I think next hour is going to be like.

I’ll publish this post, and share the link in the IWCB group. Then I’ll close my laptop, and brush my teeth. I’ll prepare for tomorrow morning’s run, and go lie down in the bed. I may browse some social media and/or feeds for a while, and fall asleep soon afterward.

This has been a day in my life.

Some numbers from today:

  • Steps walked: 11238
  • Distance walked: 7.5km
  • Distance traveled: 33km
  • Water intake: 3.55l

entry.title: Chandrayaan 3’s rigorous Moon landing approach reminds us of the testing regime key to future global success in space
entry.content:
On August 23, 2023 at 12:33 UTC, India’s robotic Chandrayaan 3 robotic lander completed the 19 minutes of its nerve-wracking autonomous descent to the Moon. In one piece and upright, it now lay near the lunar south pole at the coordinates 69.37°S, 32.32°E. The triumphant touchdown made India only the fourth nation to achieve the feat of a soft lunar landing, following the former Soviet Union, the US, and China. Success wasn’t a given, especially considering that four out of the previous five lunar landing attempts had failed: namely the Israel-based SpaceIL’s Beresheet craft, India’s own Chandrayaan 2 lander, private Japanese firm ispace’s Hakuto-R, and Russia’s Luna 25.

Launched by ISRO about four years after Chandrayaan 2’s crash on the Moon, Chandrayaan 3 saw the agency pursue and clinch its goal with a completely different approach. “Instead of a success-based design, ISRO has this time opted for a failure-based design,” said ISRO’s then-Chief S. Somanath during a press briefing. Chandrayaan 3 focused on all that can fail, and how those failures can be prevented. “We looked at sensor failure, engine failure, algorithm failure, calculation failure,” added Somanath. But when the mission’s LVM3 rocket, the Chandrayaan 3 spacecraft’s mass across its modules, and the mission’s budget as approved by the Indian government all remained roughly the same as Chandrayaan 2, how can redundancies against failures be built in for the second attempt?

This is where the Chandrayaan 2 orbiter comes in, which has been operating nominally in lunar orbit since 2019 and mapping the Moon with its many instruments. The orbiter had ended up with ample fuel margin after carrying the Chandrayaan 2 lander from Earth orbit to lunar orbit in 2019. Because of its good performance, ISRO figured it could lend some of the Chandrayaan 3 orbiter’s mass to the lander instead, which includes fuel reserves.

The 1752-kilogram Chandrayaan 3 lander, named Vikram after the originator of the Indian space program Vikram Sarabhai, was 280 kilograms heavier than its predecessor. This provided greater redundancy, such as more fuel to better stay on its intended trajectory onto the lunar surface, strengthened legs to absorb the mechanical shocks of touchdown, extended solar panels to ensure power generation in more orientations post-landing, a new velocity sensor for enhanced navigation measurements during descent, and software improvements to accommodate sensor failures. “Getting the reconfigured lander as a robust system on paper itself was crucial because you can’t really redo hardware in advanced development phases. This is where Chandrayaan 2’s flight was invaluable. Its many in-house developed systems that did work allowed us to arrive at a Chandrayaan 3 configuration that wasn’t overdone,” said Kalpana Kalahasti, the mission’s Associate Project Director, during an interview I conducted for Nature.

Kalahasti and Project Director Palanivel Veeramuthuvel led the mission through ISRO’s Bangalore-based U R Rao Satellite Center (URSC), which integrated the Chandrayaan 3 spacecraft by coordinating with various ISRO centers and suppliers across the nation. Kalahasti and Veeramuthuvel said they spent the bulk of Chandrayaan 3’s development time coming up with and overseeing comprehensive ground tests to increase the likelihood of a safe landing. These efforts spanned testing landing sensors on a helicopter to mimic different descent phases, examining the performance of engines which need to dynamically throttle, and assessing the navigation system’s ability to avoid hazards before touchdown using crane-based setups on Moon-like terrain. ISRO also conducted lander leg drop tests on lunar simulant beds and other surfaces to ensure it can handle varied slopes and a range of velocities during the crucial moment of touchdown. The agency developed a lunar soil simulant called LSS-ISAC-1 by sourcing naturally occurring, Moon-like anorthositic rock fragments from the Sittampundi Anorthosite Complex in southern India. This aided the simulant’s fidelity, and therefore built confidence in the hardware test results translating to success when at the real Moon.

ISRO then topped off the efforts with another measure. “You can only go so far with hardware tests. You can’t subject hardware to many failure scenarios, and so we formed a dedicated simulation group to characterize our lander’s ability to recover from off-nominal trajectories,” added Kalahasti. This group also simulated each redundant path the lander could’ve taken during autonomous descent to be confident about the desired outcome.

Lunar descent, mode autonomous

Chandrayaan 3’s entire lunar descent had to be fully autonomous. During this crucial stage of the mission, signals take about three seconds to go from the lander to Earth and back again—a delay too long for earthbound ISRO engineers to reliably guide the landing. So Vikram’s task was to reduce its high orbital velocity to zero, such that it stays as close to its intended trajectory as possible all the way until a soft touchdown. To do so, it needed to orchestrate the firing of its engines based on continuous measurements of distance, velocity, and orientation. Chandrayaan 3’s guidance, navigation, and control abilities were thus improved. “There were improvements to 21 subsystems for Chandrayaan 3. These changes have been reinforced by numerous helicopter- and crane-based ground tests,” said Nilesh Desai, the then-director of ISRO’s Space Applications Center (SAC) in Ahmedabad, for an article I wrote for Scientific American.

Vikram’s roughly 19-minute-long lunar descent comprised four major phases. The first, the “rough braking” phase, began when the spacecraft was 30 kilometers above the Moon in its orbit and about 750 kilometers downrange from its landing site. By firing all of its four 800-newton main engines for about 12 minutes until it was at a 7-kilometer altitude, Chandrayaan 3 reduced its high horizontal velocity of about 1.7 kilometers/second by some 80 percent. Next up came a brief but crucial 10-second “attitude hold” phase, wherein the lander stabilized itself using its eight smaller thrusters to gain a steady view of the looming lunar surface for its various landing sensors. Here, Chandrayaan 3 could throttle its engines and correct deviations from its intended trajectory more quickly than Chandrayaan 2.

For height measurements, Chandrayaan 3 relied on two altimeters, one using lasers and the other using microwaves. While laser altimeters are commonly employed by several lunar landers, they can be prone to failures or report anomalous heights at times if, say, a lander passes over a mountainous terrain or a large crater. Dysfunctional altimeters have led to crashed landings for ispace Japan’s first and second Mooncraft as well as hard landings for US-based Intuitive Machine’s IM-1 and IM-2 missions, all in this decade itself. Chandrayaan 3 would benefit from a redundancy here. Unlike laser rangefinders, “the microwave altimeter’s wider footprint allowed Chandrayaan 3 to better tolerate abrupt changes in altitude,” explained Priyanka Mehrotra of SAC, who was the lead system designer of Chandrayaan 3’s Ka-Band microwave altimeter.

Chandrayaan 3’s lander also used a new instrument called a Laser Doppler Velocimeter (LDV) to navigate more precisely in the first place. “While there are other ways for a lunar lander to measure its velocity, an LDV provides a direct measurement with respect to the ground, which allows a lander to greatly reduce accumulation of navigation errors,” said William Coogan, lunar lander chief engineer at Firefly Aerospace, a US-based company which landed the Blue Ghost spacecraft on the Moon for NASA’s CLPS program later in 2025. However, in a post-landing interview with Republic World, Somanath said that Chandrayaan 3’s descent and landing went so nominally that the LDV didn’t end up being necessary. The development nevertheless enables ISRO to use the advanced sensor on upcoming missions like Chandrayaan 4 sample return and Chandrayaan 5 / LUPEX, which have greater precision requirements.

After the attitude hold phase, Chandrayaan 3 entered a three-minute “fine braking” phase in which it used only two of its four main engines to descend up to roughly 850 meters above the Moon’s surface. It then briefly hovered there, so as to capture pictures of the surface and compare them to preloaded onboard satellite images to determine whether it was above its desired landing region. The preloaded maps were primarily sourced from the Chandrayaan 2 orbiter and NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO). High-resolution images from them were also used to select Chandrayaan 3’s landing site. “The target landing zone spans 4 by 2.5 kilometers. ISRO scientists and engineers divided it into 3900 equal-sized subsections, meticulously assessed the safety level of each for a landing, and loaded it into the lander as reference information,” noted Desai.

Triumphant touchdown

After hovering over the surface and comparing snapped images to preloaded maps, the Vikram lander determined that it was indeed above the intended landing zone. Its onboard computer then identified the safest feasible subsection area and accordingly proceeded toward touchdown. Had Vikram found itself elsewhere, it would’ve still proceeded with an autonomous landing but based on self-identified hazard levels from captured imagery instead of a predetermined subsection.

In the final “terminal descent” phase, Chandrayaan 3 lowered itself to about 150 meters above the surface and then hovered again for about half a minute to assess the area below for landing hazards. At this point, since the surface right below the lander didn’t look safe, the lander sought a safer adjacent area and deviated to touchdown there. “The processing system for hazard avoidance was sped up for Chandrayaan 3 to make the lander’s decision-making during the critical final phases significantly faster than Chandrayaan 2,” said Rinku Agrawal of SAC, who led the team that developed the processing unit of the hazard detection and avoidance system.

Finally, Chandrayaan 3 made contact with the Moon’s surface. Sensors on the lander’s legs detected the same and triggered the shutdown of its main engines. ISRO designed the legs to absorb most of the mechanical shock from the touchdown. The agency’s leg design tests on lunar simulant test beds on Earth ensured that the lander could tolerate a high vertical velocity of three meters per second—and even a horizontal velocity of one meter per second if it were to touch down askew. Vikram’s touchdown was smooth, hitting the surface with a vertical velocity of 0.983 meters/second, notably less than the nominally expected upper bound of 2 meters/second. The final location of 69.37°S, 32.32°E placed Chandrayaan 3 just ~350 meters away from its targeted ideal spot.

Chandrayaan 3’s landing was the most pole-ward at the time. The near-polar lunar surface and environment had never been measured in-situ before Chandrayaan 3 arrived. Chandrayaan 3 was intentionally landed a day after local dawn to maximize the solar-powered lander and rover’s surface operations lifetime to most of the lunar daylight period of 14 Earth days. ISRO powered on the lander’s three active instruments on August 24, each of which returned valuable data for 11 days since. From August 25, the rover began exploring the geologically rich landing region and traversed 100 meters on the lunar surface over 10 Earth days. As usual, r/ISRO subreddit admin u/Ohsin had compiled a detailed rundown of post-landing events, something which ISRO did not adequately, contextually provide or even list later on in one place. Three years after Chandrayaan 3’s lunar surface operations, science from the mission has grounded our understanding of a distinct region on the Moon just as we prepare to send a wave of lunar missions.

Meticulous Moonshot

Chandrayaan 3 should be remembered for how the team meticulously emerged from failure. Moon landings remain hard even on retries, evident by the failed soft landing of Intuitive Machines’ second lunar lander IM-2 and the crash of ispace Japan’s second Hakuto-R craft, both flying after Chandrayaan 3 and within two years of their respective first missions. At a critical time, Chandrayaan 3 kept the momentum for the Moon going by feeding into the global frenzy of sending robotic missions to Luna for long-term space exploration. “India giving the hard problem of a lunar landing a second try soon after its first attempt is an appreciated investment the whole world will benefit from,” said Jessy Kate Schingler, an outer space policy researcher and a senior advisor at the Open Lunar Foundation (a Moon Monday sponsor).

Chandrayaan 3’s tedious developmental efforts evidently paid off. However, conducting so many tests and integrating their results while also working towards the flight model was a giant, iterative task. Swiftly coordinating the dozen ISRO centers involved countrywide wasn’t easy. “It was as if we were building five to six different satellites together,” remarked Kalahasti. To take on the responsibility, Kalahasti leaned on her past experiences in project management and systems engineering, which notably included leading roles in ISRO’s Earth observation satellites such as the Indo-French SARAL craft. “The goal was to have a well documented, well understood system. There was no compromise in demonstrating the system’s performance down to its specifics,” said Kalahasti, who represents not just herself but Mehrotra, Agrawal, the over 100 such women who worked on the mission, and the nation-wide Chandrayaan 3 team. India now celebrates August 23 as National Space Day.

The world is now mounting numerous Moon missions to directly explore the treacherous lunar south pole and its water ice. In this new frontier, Chandrayaan 3’s rigorous testing approach must remain a reminder of not leaving success to chance as much as possible. There is another important reason to remember Chandrayaan 3. The country is facing an orbital launch crisis this decade and next while its national needs and ambitions have scaled and spanned across the spectrum. And so the time is here again to reinforce, scale, and apply Chandrayaan 3’s diligence to the most fundamental technology driving space activities.

The article is a synthesized and edited composition of my coverage of Chandrayaan 3 across Moon Monday, Scientific American, Nature, and Indian Space Progress, done so to provide a complete picture of the most critical aspect of the mission: the nail-biting descent and landing.

entry.title: OpenNIC Exploration Oct 2026
entry.content:
Some experiments with alternate DNS system

Yesterday Badri asked on CoDeMa:

What do you think of setting up OpenNIC based DNS lookups on servers hosting FSCI operated services?

It prompted me to try out opennic myself.

The thread actually links to FSCI’s guide to using OpenNIC on android.

For my computer though, I used the opennic-up script that I discovered from OpenNIC Wiki. (It is available on AUR).

With that set up, I was able to browse through some listed sites like be.libre.

Registering

be.libre was broken many times while I was trying to register, but I was finally able to take akshay.geek and point it to my nameserver. On my bind nameserver, I just added a new zone for akshay.geek and started serving the DNS. For caddy, I just did

http://akshay.geek {
  respond "Hi"
}

And although it took some time for the DNS to propagate, it actually started working after a while.

I tried registering on .o as well (http://akshay.o). The dot.o registry was working very well, and even had an https mirror at https://dot-o.eo.gl/. But after registering akshay.o, it had been in pending state for a few hours. I got impatient and emailed the support mail, and got it activated.

HTTPS

While investigating certificates I realized that caddy even can act as an ACME server itself. Anyhow, for TLS to be meaningful, everyone should install a common root CA certificate and the one in the wiki (playground.acme.libre) seems to be down and therefore there’s no point in trying for TLS. Although, with caddy it would have been as easy as (maybe):

akshay.geek {
  tls {
    issuer acme {
      dir https://playground.acme.libre/directory
    }
  }
}

Discovering sites

The search engine grep.geek was being intermittenly offline. And I couldn’t find any interesting sites on the OpenNIC TLDs. So I set out to find some on my own.

I knew that Tier 1 DNS servers could do zone transfer from OpenNIC root DNS servers. So I figured that these would be public and I could just do the zone transfer on my computer (which I could). Thus I ran the following commands to get some domains from .geek TLD:

$ dig @ns2.opennic.glue. geek AXFR > geek

There are many results, but many sites are also offline. So I ran the following command to make curl see if they’re up and healthy (with a three second timeout).

$ for f in $(awk '{print $1}' geek | uniq); do echo "$f" && curl --fail --out-null --connect-timeout 3 $f && echo $f >> geek-valid ; done

Then I removed duplicates with

$ sort --unique geek -o geek

Now, I added http:// etc in zed’s multiline editing (although I could have figured out doing that with awk or something) and opened the valid links in firefox with:

entry.title: Weeknote September 28 - October 5 2026
entry.content:
Heyo new weeknote and this has been an eventful week.

The tides are turning against unemployment as we speak. I am getting interviews and take home assignments. I guess when you expect nothing you will be pleasently surprised.

Besides that the big and notable highlights of my week were watching my friend perform her drum performance for the first time, attending my first indie gamedev playtest meetup and also working on my blog with weblog an inititative started by Jatan to make a small and dedicated in person community around blogging.

I will elaborate on the Indie game playtest meet because this was my first one. I am not extrovert by any means but that day I had to extrovert out of all my pores which was quite exhausting and rewarding. I got to meet so many people working on such interesting projects. Let me share it in the order which I remember.

Firstly it was a game which has been tentatively titled "License to Kill" which is inspired by Hotline Miami and the works of Suda51. They are wearing their inspirations on their sleeves and I love it. I used to think that I would never run into people who loved hotline miami as much as I do or are familiar with the ouvre of Grasshopper Manufacture but I was happy to be proved wrong on this one. All the best to them and I hope that we can have a longer conversation about their game.

Next is a game tentatively titled "Project Gilgamesh" this was the one which had a huge queue for the playtest. It is a rhythm based parkour game which you have to play to get the feel for. The artstyle was very polished and my compliments especially to the person incharge of the level assets. If I had to describe the art it is something like the works of Heart Machine aka Hyper Light Drifter or it's more 3D counterpart Hyper Light Breaker.

Another game which I had a lot of fun playing was this co-op game called spook a boo which has a demo out now and will be releasing sometime next year. It is also really polished and super fun to play. If I had to describe it, it's artstlyle is Luigi's Mansion meets the gameplay of Overcooked. So a nice couch co-op ghostbusting session, which is fun for the whole family.

I also played a game tentatively titled "pen fight" which is still very early in development, and the Dev is actively seeking player feedback to improve the experience. I would say fans of the old Beyblade GBA games should be on the lookout for this one.

One of the more interesting games which I played was a physical card game called Brew. It is a four person deck builder where you draw potion ingredients from the deck and build potions from them to score points. The interesting mechanics come in the form of:

  1. The ingredients will decay at the end of the round, and potions made with decayed ingredients will lose points.

  2. There are player archetypes which have an effect on the play space for example I played the alchemist which lets me use the effect of one potion twice.

The player archetypes are unique and seem inspired by Slay the Spire, and I want to encourage the dev to make it more deliciously devious in the PVP aspects. Hopefully I can have another round when the next session happens.

There were also other games which i couldn't get around to on time but I had so much fun talking and feeling inspired by the devs who are working on their games. I wish them all a very multi-million dollars in their bank account.

The weblog session was spontaneous because I got to know that the session was happening 10 mins before it actually started. So I had to rush all the way across town to make it.

The session was great and I am looking forward to making it on time to the next one. I arrived unfashionably late but still in time to bang out a blog and have it be critiqued by someone with editorial intent. I love the idea of taking my writing more seriously and having it be read by someone with the editorial eye as it will only help me improve which is one step on my multi-step plan towards world domination.

entry.title: (#2026-W39) far from home, far from hugs
entry.content:
I’ve felt tired a lot lately. ¶

I was going to write a long (forcefully) morose weeknote about how hard it is to find companionship and how I feel a little touch-starved when I’m not home. I still am writing about all this, but I’m not going to be as pitiful about it, because I’ve realized I feel more irritation in this regard than I feel sadness. ¶

I am clear in the belief that my love language revolves around giving gifts, acts of service and physical touch. I like making other people comfortable or giving them joy; not in a people-pleasing way, but more so “I want to show this person they’re loved and make them feel happy, so I will.” ¶

I have showcased love in this way; to friends, to family, and (sometimes but not that much) to crushes. I have seen people happy and it has made me happy. But what I’m realizing more and more lately is that I want care and love in return. I want the policy of, “Give the love you want to receive,” to be applied completely. My problem is with that receiving part. ¶

Now to be clear, people do reciprocate. My family most of all; there are many hugs and warm dinners and gifts back home. When Kinder-Joy was doing their Batman toys, my sister took her normal Batman and painted it gold to match the rare Batman from that series. She gifted it to me, and it is sitting on my dressing table looking at me as I write this, my superior protector. ¶

The problem though is that I’m not at home right now. I’m in Bangalore. And I’ve noticed I don’t get very many hugs while I’m in Bangalore. There’s many hangouts and meetups and talking to friends and new people. But this hugs part has been quite a bother for me this week. I don’t know why. ¶

To my friends, please don’t hug me if you don’t want to! I’m just blabbering here.

Also, you know those moments where you recall something cringe you did in the past, and suddenly wince? I usually have those when I’m stepping more out of my comfort zone and meeting new people. And I’ve been having more of those lately. ¶

Maybe that’s what it is. I feel like I’m reaching out to a lot of new people and not always receiving the attention I’m putting in. That deficiency of reciprocation might be what’s getting on my nerves slowly. I don’t think I’m doing too much, but maybe it would be better to cocoon for a bit. ¶

I also think it’s because of being on social media more, because I’m seeing a lot more happy lives and people celebrating wins I dream of. I do have a lot, and I have gratitude for it, but seeing sunshine and rainbows so much and then coming back to a quiet, dimly lit room might not be good for me anyway. ¶

Some people have also been telling me in passing that, now that my employment is taken care of, “I just need to find a girlfriend.” I really don’t like the idea of looking at companionship as a box to tick, but I did feel the yearning for it myself too. I’m wondering now if that yearning wouldn’t linger as much if I had more hugs. Is it all hugs in the end? ¶

As I finish writing, I’m sitting in the office cafeteria on my break. When I go back to my accommodation after work, I will lie down for a while before I exercise and work on some code before I sleep. I might video-call home and wish everyone goodnight. But maybe I still wish a little to have someone next to me to say goodnight to, too. ¶

Okay the writing is getting cringe now. I’m going to stop right here. ¶

Regularly scheduled programming (and my shenanigans from IndiaFOSS) will be included in the next weeknote. Between IndiaFOSS and all the other things I do in that week, it’s going to be a long one. :) ¶

Thank you for reading through, and if you want to force melancholy today I’m going to recommend listening to Freakin’ Out On the Interstate by Briston Maroney and Love Me Like There’s No Tomorrow by Freddie Mercury. Peace. ¶

entry.title: Weeknotes: Week #40 (2026)
entry.content:
This week was super fun as I got the chance to meet my colleagues for the first time in weeks, played a ton more of CONTROL: Resonant, and watched two movies!

Social

Fenil pitched Yash and me on a breakfast place nearby, except we chose to go there on Tuesday. Guess the one day in the week they are closed :)

To celebrate Cloudflare’s 16th birthday, we had a team dinner at the Hilton hotel in Embassy GolfLinks. It was nice to chat with everyone again after nearly a month of not having an office. We were given a soft promise of the new office reopening some time in the next 5 to 10 days 🤞. I’m eagerly looking forward to getting some time in there before I leave for home at the end of the month.

Following up on the promise to myself made during the last IndieWebClub, I chose to go a little early to hang out with people; I had a great time yapping with Ankur and a few others who shall go unnamed purely because I am terrible with names 😓

The discussions at IWC itself were quite spirited and engaging. Apparently we all have a lot of strong opinions on archiving! Could be fun to have another session dedicated purely towards it. I ended up using the writing time to delete some drafts instead of working on them, so admittedly the spirit of that exercise was a little lost on me.

Media

Writing

I published a post about my IndiaFOSS 2026 experience which got reposted by the CEO of FOSS United, admittedly a nice surprise :)

Reading

I finished reading Wheel of the Infinite and picked up When We Cease to Understand The World purely because it was in my eBook collection, having no clue what the theme was. The premise was a bit of a shock, but it’s quite intriguing and rather short, so I’ll read it through.

Movies

Yash and I watched two movies this week: Digger starring Tom Cruise and Primetime starring Robert Pattinson.

Digger was deeply weird and often hard to follow, but Tom Cruise really delivers something unique here that we haven’t seen in a long, long while from him. I could go for a re-watch of this today and still have as much fun as I did.

Primetime is significantly less weird, but delivers just as much on the acting front. Robert Pattinson has proved time and again that he’s a phenomenal actor and this was no different. His Chris Hansen is deeply troubled, an obvious hypocrite, and just as fucked up as someone trying to convert paedophilia into TV views would be. Aftermath had an in-depth breakdown of the movie that I quite enjoyed reading and resonated with me.

Games

CONTROL: Resonant still has me fully hooked, and I’ve been making steady progress on it all week. I got through two Resonant fights; the Factory Resonant fight was extremely telegraphed and barely had anything to it, so I one-shot it with ease. The Park Resonant was much more fun, and I had to take a few shots at it before I finally got it down. On my final attempt I was so locked in that I forgot to blink and my eyes started burning to remind me of the fact. I need to take this stuff less seriously!

Personal Projects

Somewhat unsurprisingly, last week’s Claw release got rejected by the IzzyOnDroid repository for its new proprietary dependency on Play Core, so I had to create a separate FOSS-only build to satisfy their requirements again. The team behind IzzyOnDroid do great work on extending the core F-Droid repository with apps that are still FOSS but might have some other properties that make them unsuitable for core. I’ve donated to them in the past and would encourage others to do the same!

This site received some very minor tweaks; footnotes now render as popovers on the website (like this1), the dark theme for code blocks was changed, and the WebMentions server was tweaked to make it possible to provide per-host renderers so I can tweak how, say, bubbles.town webmentions show up under my posts.

🤖 CLANK CLANK CLANK 🤖

Yash and I use an app called Spliit to manage our shared transactions for the household. I discovered recently that it has an in-built JSON and CSV export, so I added support in factual-budget to generate a summary of unsettled transactions with proper categories.

Cooking

Being at home all week has made cooking much easier, so we’re now cooking most days.

entry.title: Sometimes art is like a wild fire
entry.content:
I had the pleasure of watching one of my best friends do something new on 2nd October.

She picked up the hobby of drumming which is fairly random, but if you know her it tracks.

We arrived at the venue as the performances were in full swing. These are all people who are in their late twenties or older following their passions in singing and playing musical instruments. There is something beautiful in people trying to find their passions later in life, because it gives me a glimpse into what they could have been if they had been provided the resources to pursue their interests as opposed to being cogs in a machine which converts human resources into shareholder value.

My friend is a new mom, so it goes without saying that I am proud of the fact that she has not only managed the delicate process of nurturing an actual new human in this world but also not lost her own individuality in that endeavor. A lot of that has to do with the fact that she has a supportive partner who makes sure to take care of the mental load and in some cases take over when she needs him to without her having to ask him to.

I have just seen small snippets of her playing the drums on instagram, never seen her play the full thing and I didn't even know the song which she has selected. Now armed with her phone camera I am seated in the front row like an eager parent excited for their kids first performance.

The first funny thing which happens when my friend gets on stage is that my niece aka my friends child lets out a bone chilling, spine curling shriek. She has seen her mother and needs her like people need oxygen.

Her husband has to do the unfortunate thing of taking his child out of the auditorium, meaning that he will be missing her performance live. This is one of the realities of parenting sometimes you will have to sacrifice things to make sure someone else is happy. Therefore the pressure is on me to make sure that the video I take is steady and clear so that they can relive the performance as many times as necessary with the knowledge that it will never live up to the real thing. No pressure, obviously.

The song is "Rolling in the deep by Adele" She will be drumming to the song, making sure to keep the beat.

What follows is basically best described as a beautiful wild fire. Because she is playing the drums it is the most exciting performance of the night by virtue of being the most loud. As humans there is something primal about percussion, hence the overwhelming response to beats on a drum.

I can tell that she has been practicing this song for a few months now. Initially it is almost perfectly on the beat. Elevating the vocals of the song. The lights are going crazy, the fog machine is setting a mood. The audience sits quietly enraptured by the percussion. She is lost in the rhythm, it is exciting watching someone perform with true passion.

I can imagine a future where she keeps this up and is able to do a solo without needing a background track or a past where this is her hobby and it lets her make friends easier by being one of the cool kids in the rock band.

She starts rushing her beats in the middle, you can tell that she has a tendency to interpret the song at a faster pace than it actually is. But it doesn't matter. This is her first performance in front of a crowd which is already an achievement because overcoming stage fright is something most people can't do. Besides, perfection can only be achieved for one moment, and she has already done that during the first portion of the song.

Recovering her pace, she keeps the beat and winds down the song to applause. People loved her performance, of course she has not a lot of time to take in the applause. She has to go and check in on her child and husband who could not watch it with her. That's also a reality check in being a parent.

It is fun to watch someone who is still honing their craft, you can see the areas which they have nailed and the areas which they will eventually perfect. Watching people pursue creative interests is something which I personally love because you never know what is someone's true calling. Maybe drumming is the thing she will find the most joy in and be creatively satiated, maybe this will be the small spark that will be the actual wild fire of new creative ways to express herself.

I hope that eventually when her kid grows up enough to have opinions she chooses to be passionate like her mother, and makes art she is passionate about instead of losing herself in this weird capitalist hellscape. I hope to encourage her weird art whether it be finger painting the mona lisa with ketchup and chocolate sauce. As long as she is happy making things.

That is all that matters.

entry.title: My house has a chokehold over me!
entry.content:
and my perfect schedule does not stand a chance.

I had a plan for how I wanted to start October. My house had some inputs on said plan.

Things have been breaking around my house for the last couple of days. Extension cords shot, a water purifier out of action, and many electronics going through their moody teenage phase.

AArpit3 Oct

i have not checked the data, so don’t quote me on it.

A couple of days ago in Bangalore, we had what felt like the heaviest rain of the year. It started pouring in the evening, paused briefly, then returned for a thunderous night.

Anyway, September ended, and I am awake now – apparently for electrical repairs.

October felt important because life has been changing quite a bit for me lately. A while ago, I decided to step away from organising VizChitra after helping run the conference for two years. Also after two years, my role at work is evolving into a more favourable shape.

These changes have opened up a lot of time in my life, and I have been asking myself what I want my days to look like going forward and, most importantly, how to make room to create for myself again.

As a way to explore this creativity again, I have been reading The Artist’s Way with a friend and doing the weekly exercises (keep an eye out for the weekly series on it). I felt committed to October as the beginning of this shift in my life, with a little more space for myself to be.

Instead, the start of the month has been choppy and tiring. My house had its own plans for the month, and it did not feel like informing me about them.

I keep wanting to treat all of this like a regular interruption, fix what needs fixing, then get back to my day. But I am increasingly unsure that if one ever truly “gets back to their day.” while also inhabiting a house.

AArpit3 Oct

the constant anticipation.

There is always another fix waiting in the wings: a fan that starts clicking in the middle of a call, the cabinet hinge that suddenly wants to squeak. My attention has been permanently half-parked on just looking after the house for years.

I am not sure there was ever a stretch when the house didn’t need something. I cannot even remember many conversations from my childhood with my parents, where repairs were not a part of it.

And then there are the jobs I have invented for myself. My magnum opus is reorganising the bookshelf every six months. Either because the books on my shelves have changed, or the way I organise them in my head has shifted, so the bookshelf feels like it needs to reflect that.

Nobody is making me do that one. I just want the shelves to make sense again!

I could blame my current predicament on the limitations of this particular house, or maybe if I had more money for someone to take care of everything full-time I would not feel this. On a tiring day like the one I just had, both explanations are tempting.

But I love this house. I do not particularly want a bigger one. And I especially do not want to hand over all the looking after it, either. I like doing things myself, knowing where things are, deciding how they should work, making this place feel like mine.

I just wish it did not get so overwhelming sometimes.

Some of this feeling of being overwhelmed probably comes from how I plan my days. I fill them to the brim, assigning every available bit of time to something I want to do. There’s very little room for ambiguity. Certainly no slot labelled “water purifier not purifying”.

And when something breaks, I stop and deal with it – because that’s what living in a house requires, and because I care about this one.

I am tired at the end of all the fixes, and annoyed that I have not done what I planned, even though I have spent the day doing something that matters to me.

I do not have a neat conclusion, and not looking for solutions, either. Maybe I just want things to stop breaking for a while and catch a breath.

One thing I would appreciate is a significant amount of uninterrupted time reading, writing, or making things.

But I think I need to leave a little more room in my plans for the home I actually live in. Including the inconvenient parts of looking after it. I love this house. Sometimes I would like for it to love me back by keeping all its appliances working. For now, I will settle for a functioning water purifier.
